To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of lamivudine for prophylaxis against HBV reactivation during chemotherapy is safe, effective and should be considered as a routine practice for HBsAg positive patients with hematologic malignancy.
The use of a combination of lamivudine and prednisolone for HBV reactivation in patients with hematological malignancies is effective, safe and well tolerated.

1) the incidence of HBV reactivation in patients with solid tumors receiving chemotherapy is 3% to 10%; 2) HBV reactivation is associated with a high rate of morbidity and mortality; and 3) prophylactic lamivudine treatment significantly decreases the rate of HBV reactivity and the associated complications.
